reviews.text: The Trial of the Chicago 7 is a story dripping in mythos, yet teeming with incredible humanity, with a power that more than carries across the five decades between then and now: folklore inseparable from the world today.
reviews.author: Harry Solomons

reviews.text: It’s a perfectly functional re-enactment of events that lacks grace and subtlety. It references history, but only for lip service, making everything feel removed and lacking context.
reviews.author: Joonatan Itkonen

reviews.text: The Trial of the Chicago 7 is Aaron Sorkin at his finest, and I hope the next project he does has as much passion and heart in it as this does.
reviews.author: Ryan McQuade

reviews.text: With such a compelling story and quick, sharp editing to match the screenplay, this is a worthy film for my top ten of the year.
reviews.author: Amy Smith

reviews.text: Mark Rylance proves to us why that surprise Oscar win was well deserved
reviews.author: Jillian Chilingerian

reviews.text: Sorkin strains to abbreviate that long arc of the moral universe, flexing it toward justice through the sheer force of sophistry and righteous indignation.
reviews.author: PJ Grisar

reviews.text: Maintaining the focus on a single location is an exceptional decision for a movie where words are the action of the story. Inside the courtroom is where every fascinating argument ensues, never losing steam until the very end.
reviews.author: Manuel São Bento

reviews.text: Sorkin had to navigate more than a handful of characters, yet somehow he managed to give each of them momentum. Even characters in supporting roles are nuanced and well-developed.
reviews.author: Akos Peterbencze

reviews.text: The Trial of the Chicago 7 is a studious, accessible, intense courtroom drama that compares favorably to historically great courtroom dramas like To Kill a Mockingbird, 12 Angry Men, and Judgment at Nuremberg.
reviews.author: Wesley Lovell

reviews.text: Captures the exact spirit of the end of the hippie era. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Erick Estrada

reviews.text: If you find yourself on the idealistic end of the spectrum, The Trial of the Chicago 7 is a film that is made for the masses. It applies the classic Hollywood treatment to its worthy subject matter
reviews.author: M.N. Miller

reviews.text: Sorkin writes a very white hat/black hat tale that leaves practically nothing for us to wrestle with. Still, he’s a good enough writer to energize the many characters and tell a mesmerizing story even if it’s only a subjective CliffsNotes version.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: It is good to see that the creator of the inimitable Borat and Ali G demonstrate that his range extends to characters who might melt into everyday society.
reviews.author: Jane Freebury

reviews.text: While the term important film is overused, The Trial of the Chicago 7 is one of the years essential must-see films.
reviews.author: David Gonzalez

reviews.text: Sorkin has tapped into something. Whether it's called Capraesque or Spielbergian, the label denotes a film that accesses our emotions and ideological sympathies in simple but undeniable ways.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: The Trial of the Chicago 7 might not be the most revolutionary film of the year when it comes to thesis, but its craft and basic effectiveness is undeniable.
reviews.author: Carson Timar

reviews.text: [A] spirited and very entertaining affair...
reviews.author: Leigh Paatsch

reviews.text: As an ensemble piece, the film is exceptional, and it laments Sorkin as an interesting director, who still has much to learn in terms of visual storytelling.
reviews.author: Maria Lattila

reviews.text: Seems rushed and too close to the heart of the filmmaker to be more grounded in living history than in personal sentiment, but it has Mark Rylance to hold that balance.
reviews.author: Milana Vujkov

reviews.text: Sorkin uses this reminder for building an emotionally laden finale, one whose essence remains solid - a truth that advises remembering the past and trying to learn from it...
reviews.author: Robin Holabird

reviews.text: The Trial Of The Chicago 7 gets off to a slow start but it sucked me in and I was fixated by the end of the two-hour runtime.
reviews.author: Tilly Pearce

reviews.text: Although the film has certain narrative missteps, especially when conducting different actions in parallel, these are compensated by the usual bursts of brilliant made-in-Sorkin dialogue and by its forceful plot effects. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Alejandro G. Calvo

reviews.text: Post-1968, looking back at decades of foreign wars, mass shootings and the power of law enforcement officers to act with impunity, Sorkin's trust at best feels quaint and at worst, misguided.
reviews.author: John Lui

reviews.text: The Trial of the Chicago 7 is the worst film of the twenty-first century so far.
reviews.author: A.S. Hamrah

reviews.text: To see this racist humiliation now by the out-of-his-depth Judge Hoffman (Frank Langella) is gasp-out-loud shocking and yet sadly resonant in the present-day brutal treatment and killings of African Americans.
reviews.author: Alexa Dalby

reviews.text: The Trial of the Chicago 7 might be the ultimate movie about how to fight the far right -- an artistic testament to pragmatism and a cry of rage in the era of Donald Trump and Derek Chauvin.
reviews.author: Matthew Rozsa

reviews.text: A thrilling piece of angry social history.
reviews.author: Paul M. Bradshaw

reviews.text: Ultimately, Sorkin has created little more than slick, Hollywood hokum. But it's quite good slick Hollywood hokum.
reviews.author: Witney Seibold

reviews.text: The film is instructive, which is good. It further does an excellent job of depicting principled, high-stakes argument, which is even better.
reviews.author: Abbie Bernstein

reviews.text: ...benefits from its raft of above-average performances...
reviews.author: David Nusair

reviews.text: Evocative, and often absolutely mesmerizing.
reviews.author: Felix Vasquez Jr.

reviews.text: Inevitably we find ourselves measuring this kangaroo court against the events of the present day, when Black Lives Matter protests have raged across America
reviews.author: John McDonald

reviews.text: A lot of this film feels manufactured to me. And while the story is presented in a very comfortable way, I didn't necessarily feel like the film was as revolutionary as it thought it was.
reviews.author: Luke Parker

reviews.text: Sorkin's hand is noticeable in the structure of the film. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Hugo Hernández Valdivia

reviews.text: A film that is stylish but infuriatingly and unforgivably obtuse.
reviews.author: Laura Potier

reviews.text: ...hits enough drama pleasure centers to be suspicious.
reviews.author: Josh Larsen

reviews.text: "Bobby Seale and Fred Hampton only appear in the context of their suffering, employed as devices to brew anti-racist anger in his audience."
reviews.author: Alicja Johnson

reviews.text: In context, however, there's enough character building for these concerns to fade away, and while there's no denying this is at heart a traditional legal melodrama, it's a stirring one with the great Frank Langella in typically fine mettle...
reviews.author: Lynden Barber

reviews.text: A zippy and freewheeling piece.
reviews.author: Matt Brunson

reviews.text: ...builds tension through a series of finely-tuned arguments and monologues en route to a big, sweeping, rousing Hollywood pay-off...
reviews.author: Eddie Harrison

reviews.text: While Sorkin's work can veer from exceptional to frustrating, his second stint as a director makes the very most of his usual traits
reviews.author: Sarah Ward

reviews.text: More winning than the educational value - which is high - is the entertainment value, which gives this picture its enjoyable edge.
reviews.author: Mike Massie

reviews.text: The Trial of the Chicago 7 is a mighty - and potentially depressing - reminder of how history has a habit of repeating itself.
reviews.author: Mark Meszoros

reviews.text: The Trial of The Chicago 7 takes place in 1969; however, the film's events feel very 2020. The backdrop is a country at war, young people fighting against the establishment, and Black people fighting racism and police brutality.
reviews.author: Kathia Woods

reviews.text: The Trial of the Chicago 7 is a middle of the road crowd pleaser.
reviews.author: Eric Marchen

reviews.text: You could put this through some sort of Sorkin AI machine and it would pump out the exact same film... that said, it does crackle.
reviews.author: Simon Miraudo

reviews.text: Aaron Sorkin has an uncanny ability to make the most mundane or complicated subject matter not only palatable but entertaining.
reviews.author: Matt Neal

reviews.text: As far as courtroom dramas go, the film does a really good job to differentiate itself, going back and forth through prosecution and prosecuted events. Sorkin proves again his immense writing ability through characters and rhythm. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Victor Pineyro

reviews.text: The perfect material and cast for Sorkin and one of the strongest ensemble performances of the year.
reviews.author: Brian Gill

reviews.text: The Trial of the Chicago 7 is well worth watching, as long as one doesn't leave one's critical faculties at the door.
reviews.author: Joanne Laurier

reviews.text: Aaron Sorkin has accomplished everything he wanted and more with The Trial of the Chicago 7. It's a piece of history that deserved to be retold, and through his impeccable dialogue and direction, Sorkin has made one of the best films of the year.
reviews.author: Alex Bentley

reviews.text: This is a clean-cut, old school script that has no time for messy interludes or spare chat, but this is a feature film not a documentary and the polish adds pace.
reviews.author: Amber Wilkinson

reviews.text: It marks Sorkin's positive progression as a director. As a writer, it is arguably his best film work since A Few Good Men.
reviews.author: Grant Watson

reviews.text: From A Few Good Men to The Social Network to Moneyball and now to The Trial of the Chicago 7, no one does it like Aaron Sorkin.
reviews.author: Rhys Bowen Jones

reviews.text: The Trial of the Chicago 7 reminds us how far we think we have come in our progress, in a dazzling Aaron Sorkin fashion, only to discover that we may not have come far at all.
reviews.author: Leo Brady

reviews.text: A bridge that spans the five decades from the actual events, it's a bit of history that comments on contemporary hot-button topics like protest, civil rights, and police brutality.
reviews.author: Richard Crouse

reviews.text: What begins as a straightforward courtroom drama that must tackle a dozen complicated personalities and the legal ramifications from their decisions becomes performance art, and that momentum runs the film like a skillfully choreographed ballet.
reviews.author: Candice McMillan

reviews.text: Whether dealing with bureaucrats or student zealots, the film has a perspective on social turmoil that falls short of the insightful panorama in the French AIDS-activism epic B.P.M. Sorkin's right-side-of-history saga is the bent history.
reviews.author: Armond White

reviews.text: Glib. Forgettable. This is a Cheese Whiz movie for 12-year-olds, not for adults.
reviews.author: Cole Smithey

reviews.text: Some might critique the final product here as being a bit too Hollywood, but it's got that Frank Capra optimism that might do us all some good.
reviews.author: Cory Woodroof

reviews.text: Aaron Sorkin's sophomore effort as a director takes a humorous but honest look at one of America's most publicized trials...
reviews.author: Jennifer Heaton

reviews.text: The further we get from the '60s, the harder it is for filmmakers of Sorkin's vintage to shoehorn that decade into current events.
reviews.author: Pete Vonder Haar

reviews.text: A surprisingly well-oiled machine.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: Timely and effective. The Trial of the Chicago 7 boasts an impressive cast and an agile screenplay that gives each of them a chance to shine. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Rene Sanchez

reviews.text: Chicago 7 is a movie where the pleasures are less in the filmmaking and more in its screenplay and the cast assembled to deliver it
reviews.author: Stephen Porzio

reviews.text: Once the trial starts, the film becomes a terrific courtroom drama. The conversations between Abbie Hoffman and Hayden are brilliant.
reviews.author: Sr. Rose Pacatte

reviews.text: The Trial of the Chicago 7 might as well have been called The Showcase of Sacha Baron Cohen. Although the movie has a big ensemble cast, he ends up stealing the show in his portrayal of left-wing activist Abbie Hoffman.
reviews.author: Carla Hay

reviews.text: It works well enough, but it doesn't quite hit the ball out of the park. It is disappointing that the story doesn't stick to the facts more than it does. Sorkin puts his thumb on the scales of history too hard for my taste.
reviews.author: Robert Roten

reviews.text: Aaron Sorkin puts his trademark traits - razor-sharp wit, rhetorical flair and political insight - to very good use in this enthralling dramatisation of a notorious US trail.
reviews.author: Jason Best

reviews.text: The Trial of the Chicago 7 almost plays like a parody of Aaron Sorkin-style self-satisfaction, only it's written and directed by the real Sorkin, so it's terrible.
reviews.author: Daniel Barnes

reviews.text: While [Steve] McQueen's [Mangrove] is more internal and terrifying, [Aaron] Sorkin's [film] is self-righteous and grandstanding. But at the end of the day, both are timely given what's going on in the world today
reviews.author: Akhil Arora

reviews.text: Intentionally or not, The Trial of the Chicago 7 is an exquisite display of the white man's role in the American political and judicial systems, for better and worse.
reviews.author: Angela L. Harmon

reviews.text: The verdict should be unanimous: This is a great film.
reviews.author: Linda Cook

reviews.text: By the end, I had given myself over to the Hollywood veneer. Chicago 7 is a particularly shiny rendering of history, but Sorkin wisely places the focus on America's failings, even as he celebrates the people striving to fix them.
reviews.author: David Sims

reviews.text: The Trial of the Chicago 7 has the potential to become a bonafide crowd-pleaser that will resonate with its target demographic but reveals much room for Aaron Sorkin's political perspective to grow.
reviews.author: Diego Andaluz

reviews.text: A fascinating - albeit not entirely faithful - look at an interesting chapter from history.
reviews.author: Sameen Amer

reviews.text: As with all things Sorkin, it takes liberties with the truth - this is not a film to watch in place of reading up on the history - but it's a damn good supplement for that history, and taken as a comment on our modern justice system.
reviews.author: Tasha Robinson

reviews.text: Sorkin in Trial makes the most of big personalities and the conflicts between them. But those conflicts are manufactured debates that bear little resemblance to the real debates Americans were having then -- or are having now.
reviews.author: Megan Basham

reviews.text: The Trial of the Chicago 7 is both a courtroom drama for the ages and an urgent shot across the bows.
reviews.author: Robbie Collin

reviews.text: "The Trial of the Chicago 7" is a timely film, until the end leaves you with a bitter taste.
reviews.author: Blake Howard

reviews.text: As a director, Sorkin can barely muster any verve, portraying the highly charged atmosphere of the times with persistent flatness both in and out of the courtroom. As a writer, he cannot hope to properly capture the radical spirit of his protagonists.
reviews.author: Dan Schindel

reviews.text: If you're going to check out a courtroom drama, the best-case scenario is for Aaron Sorkin to write the screenplay. Having Sorkin direct is the third or fourth-best case scenario, however.
reviews.author: Tim Brennan

reviews.text: deeply entertaining though it may be, it is ultimately sobering in how it dramatizes not how far we might fall, but how far we have already fallen
reviews.author: James Kendrick

reviews.text: The Trial of the Chicago 7 is the ultimate Sorkin film, filled with intelligent, over-the-top characters battling within a civil structure over the ideals of America.
reviews.author: Joshua Starnes

reviews.text: This is probably one of the best-acted films that I've seen all year...and being stuck home, I've seen a LOT of movies this year...
reviews.author: Justin Brown

reviews.text: Twenty-to-thirty minutes could have been trimmed...but that's true of many Aaron Sorkin films...but I really liked the cast, and they all should be nominated...
reviews.author: Brandon Collins

reviews.text: Hoffman may be a surprise standout, a snarky class clown who becomes a voice for his fellow defendants and the war-weary nation during his closing courtroom remarks. But it's a fantastic cast in general...
reviews.author: Steve Murray

reviews.text: It is in the end nothing more than apologia, offering cheap catharsis for anyone looking to be absolved of their liberal guilt and affirmed in their squeamishness toward protest and dissent.
reviews.author: Charlotte Rosen

reviews.text: Though it doesn't quite rank as being among the most compelling of legal dramas the film nonetheless delivers a battery of punchy courtroom pyrotechnics and a cache of premium performances from an extraordinary ensemble cast.
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: With the appropriate combination between drama and irony, Sorkin shows us the incongruities of a fraudulent regime [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Gisela Savdie

reviews.text: It's weak, toothless, and wholly inadequate - both then and now.
reviews.author: Eileen Jones

reviews.text: Sorkin's film pushes all the right buttons, boasting a classic script and a dynamite cast.
reviews.author: Dan Buffa

reviews.text: Aaron Sorkin doing what he does best: a trial movie that stands on the shoulders of a historic event, supported by a massive and talented cast.
reviews.author: Alejandro Turdó

reviews.text: This is top-tier storytelling, and [Aaron] Sorkin presents the narrative with thrilling court-room drama, maddening realism and moments of levity that keep the film steadily paced and engaging throughout.
reviews.author: Kiko Martinez

reviews.text: It's a superb re-creation of that historic event, in the form of a courtroom drama.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: Special kudos go to Yahya Abdul-Mateen II in the small but significant role of the leader of the Black Panthers, Bobby Seale.
reviews.author: Diane Pershing

reviews.text: Sorkin delivers on a well-written and crowd-pleasing experience... This is a huge win for Netflix.
reviews.author: Austin Burke

reviews.text: If anyone was born to make a film about the infamous federal trial surrounding the protests outside the 1968 Democratic National Convention, it's Aaron Sorkin.
reviews.author: Lindsey Bahr

reviews.text: Courtroom drama has relevant political messages, violence.
reviews.author: Jennifer Green

reviews.text: The Trial of the Chicago 7 is a name you're going to be hearing about the deeper we go into awards season. As is often said, this isn't a perfect movie. However, the film strikes a powerful note in our contemporary climate.
reviews.author: Kimberly Pierce

reviews.text: Courtroom drama about the demonization of dissent which continues to this day.
reviews.author: Frederic and Mary Ann Brussat

reviews.text: The Trial of the Chicago 7 will stand the test of time and possibly become one of those political films that will help shape one political point of view one way or the other.
reviews.author: Alan Ng

reviews.text: Bland courtroom scenes, hokey dialogue and terrible wigs.
reviews.author: Bob Grimm

reviews.text: Thank goodness for Sorkin's gift for dialogue, since what could be overwrought becomes righteous anger, and the liberties he took go down smoother than they should.
reviews.author: Andrea Thompson

reviews.text: Chicago 7 is a crowdpleaser first and foremost, and in that regard it succeeds on almost every level... Just don't expect it to be as revolutionary as some of those it calls its heroes.
reviews.author: Angie Han

reviews.text: It's impossible not to view The Trial of the Chicago 7 through the lens of the challenges facing America at this time in history, and because of that, it's hard not to get swept up in its inspirational trappings.
reviews.author: Cynthia Vinney

reviews.text: The film is not meant to be a documentary, though, and naturally takes creative license, keeping the essence of the real life events...
reviews.author: Arionne Nettles

reviews.text: The Trial of the Chicago 7 sees Sorkin in admirable form, commanding an enormous cast and an enormous narrative with precision.
reviews.author: Andy Crump

reviews.text: The Trial of the Chicago 7 feels outright outlandish at times; more than unrealistic, it can feel as far afield from history as an episode of the Twilight Zone.
reviews.author: K. Austin Collins

reviews.text: A highly competent legal drama that's entertaining because of the cast's fluency in the ping-pong of dialogue that's an essential feature of Sorkin's scripts. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Emmanuel Báez

reviews.text: By interchangeably telling the story with various 'performed' versions of it ... Sorkin observes the surreality of our 'infotainment' age.
reviews.author: Brett McCracken

reviews.text: The Trial of the Chicago 7 has the prestige of an awards film, but that poshness creates a hollow examination of its critical historical period.
reviews.author: Matt Conway

reviews.text: A frightful reminder of the immense power of systems over us, all packaged in great writing, acting and editing that should be required viewing from now on. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jorge Rivera Rubio

reviews.text: Sometimes, life does art one better.
reviews.author: Anne Cohen

reviews.text: The bravery of the brutalized defendants is justly legendary, but the film is no self-righteous history lesson. The script is stocked with zingers, and Sorkin's depiction of patriotism curdling into fascism is visceral, not didactic.
reviews.author: Bennett Campbell Ferguson

reviews.text: The casting is brilliant and features an extremely distinguished cast. Baron Cohen is one of the standouts and his jokey, theatrical delivery is perfect for Hoffman. Strong is also appealing as he portrays Rubin as a lovable schnook.
reviews.author: Hannah Brown

reviews.text: The centrist filmmaker captures the drama of the 1960s, but tries too hard to make radicals palatable to contemporary liberals.
reviews.author: Jeet Heer

reviews.text: Even tolerably wobbly in the structure, this film comes in a time where the words 'protest' and 'conspiracy' are most heard.
reviews.author: Filipe Freitas

reviews.text: The main problem: despite its likable heroes and clear villains, The Trial of the Chicago 7 cannot bring itself to indict the system that turns the wheels of its story.
reviews.author: Joshua Rivera

reviews.text: It reminds us that the schisms first paraded on the streets of Chicago or inside an out-of-control judge's courtroom haven't gone away. If anything, they've become more dangerous.
reviews.author: Eleanor Ringel Cater

reviews.text: I'd be dishonest if I said "The Trial of the Chicago 7" wasn't engaging, though it feels a little... light. The stakes don't seem as high as they might.
reviews.author: Rob Gonsalves

reviews.text: The Trial of the Chicago 7 is an engaging enough watch, but it feels mechanical. There are plenty of political and courtroom fireworks, but it lacks a beating heart.
reviews.author: Allen Almachar

reviews.text: The movie is effective in spite of its foibles. It's an ensemble piece that tells a complex story cleanly. And even its missteps hint as to why Sorkin chose to return to this historical moment now.
reviews.author: Alissa Wilkinson

reviews.text: Despite it's stacked cast, relevant topics, and high-production value, The Trial of the Chicago 7 is too interested in portraying the facts and not enough in portraying the real-life characters at its center.
reviews.author: Karl Delossantos

reviews.text: Crackling dialogue and courtroom drama...both tense and shockingly funny.
reviews.author: Steve Crum

reviews.text: The writing was a bit grandiose and self-important, a tendency that the movie's writer-director, Aaron Sorkin, has turned into a style. But he structured the late 1960s story strategically, even if he decided not to worry about historical accuracy.
reviews.author: Matthew Gilbert

reviews.text: When the world is burning, Sorkin's stubborn insistence that rhetoric and respectability are the basis for political change is not only laughable, but incredibly baffling. The whole world is watching Aaron Sorkin, and they are waiting for him to wake up.
reviews.author: Anahit Behrooz

reviews.text: Sorkin's best script since 'The Social Network,' chockablock with hyperliterate zingers and groovy grandstanding.
reviews.author: Sean Burns

reviews.text: By reshaping this charged moment culled from somewhat recent American history in his own image, Sorkin has made The Trial of the Chicago 7 about something else entirely: himself.
reviews.author: Oliver Jones

reviews.text: The Trial Of The Chicago is an entertaining and gripping drama, but should not be taken as the whole truth.
reviews.author: Jonathan Roberts

reviews.text: Sorkin is finally coming into his own as a director. Always strong with scripts, but this had everything you'd want from a courtroom drama.
reviews.author: EJ Moreno

reviews.text: The Trial of the Chicago 7 changed the course of history; for that reason alone, it's worth a look.
reviews.author: Wendy Shreve

reviews.text: The Trial of the Chicago 7 isn't perfect, but Sorkin's reenactment of this dark historical event features outstanding performances and typically entertaining dialogue.
reviews.author: Alex McPherson

reviews.text: A historically relevant courtroom drama that dramatizes, from different points of view, the fascinating way in which activists fight behind closed doors against social injustices. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Yasser Medina

reviews.text: There's literal truth and dramatic truth, and Aaron Sorkin's film...makes up for the looseness with which it treats the former with an abundance of the latter.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: It's a wiggy movie - that is, there are a lot of wigs, a lot of beards, a lot of late-60s gear - and not a very subtle one. But it is a spectacular history lesson.
reviews.author: CJ Johnson

reviews.text: A must-see film for its captivating ensemble, engaging pacing and rousing story.
reviews.author: Shane Slater

reviews.text: Maybe the most lifeless and unengagingly self-serious feature film Sorkin has written.
reviews.author: Tim Brayton

reviews.text: [It] succeeds in making us aware of our shared humanity, and the evils which exist in any system where there is an imbalance of power.
reviews.author: Sucharita Tyagi

reviews.text: Aaron Sorkin's political tales aren't bound by history, but they're no less entertaining for it. Exhibit A? 'The Trial of the Chicago 7.'
reviews.author: Rob Hunter

reviews.text: The best possible outcome for such a high dose of Sorkin.
reviews.author: Karen Han

reviews.text: [A]n absolutely stellar cast...deep with top-tier talent....As he often does when venturing into the real world, Sorkin takes some liberties with the facts, but for the most part, the larger picture remains connected to the larger truth.
reviews.author: Allen Adams

reviews.text: Don't look to this movie when write your essay about this moment in history. Do look to this movie as great art inspired by a moment in history.
reviews.author: Robert Slack

reviews.text: An all-star cast leads Aaron Sorkin's effort to bring the stories of the men who were arrested during the 1968 Democratic National Convention and charged with inciting a riot.
reviews.author: Michelle Jaworski

reviews.text: If it's simply [viewed as] a courtroom drama, it's a very good one.
reviews.author: Sean Collier

reviews.text: The meat of the film certainly does become the Hayden/Hoffman conflict, especially for those of us old enough to recognize and remember the over-amplified events in the early going.
reviews.author: John Urbancich

reviews.text: Sorkin's penchant for speechifying turns out to be perfect for a show trial that's being treated half as a circus and half as a soap box... It helps that everyone in this film is firing on all cylinders.
reviews.author: Ani Bundel

reviews.text: This is a much more polished directing effort from Sorkin... In a sense he has returned to a space where he feels comfortable.
reviews.author: Alci Rengifo

reviews.text: Aaron Sorkin's incisive courtroom drama is a showcase for the superb acting ensemble.
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: The Trial of the Chicago 7 suffers from a lack of nuances in the analysis of power... but the power of the message and the efficiency of the delivery prevail over the weaker narrative passages. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ruben Peralta Rigaud

reviews.text: The selection of actors for each role is perfect. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Pablo O. Scholz

reviews.text: "Good" and "Evil" get stamped on every character's forehead, and cuteness reigns, even though being cute and being indignant are two impulses that tend to cancel each other out... In Sorkin's hands, history becomes sitcom.
reviews.author: Kyle Smith

reviews.text: There's a fine line between topicality and self-aggrandizing opportunism, and for all of the talent on display, The Trial of the Chicago 7 stumbles along it with two left feet...
reviews.author: Adam Nayman

reviews.text: What ought to have been a captivating clash of wits and ideologies amounts to little more than standard speechifying.
reviews.author: Prahlad Srihari

reviews.text: [Sorkin] has taken "the most important trial of your lifetime" and shoehorned it into a conventional Sorkin-esque mold, one in which complicated real-life people have become narrative conventions in a movie full of character types and glib dialogue.
reviews.author: John Anderson

reviews.text: It's a notable film that may have benefitted from another director behind the camera. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Mikel Zorrilla

reviews.text: The Trial of the Chicago 7 is ultimately entertaining and timely, boasted by an incredible ensemble cast (including the talented Mark Rylance).
reviews.author: Mae Abdulbaki

reviews.text: "The Trial of the Chicago 7" will entice audiences with its clever script, an incredible cast and relevant story---easily one of the best films of 2020
reviews.author: Rosa Parra

reviews.text: Director-writer Aaron Sorkin's wickedly Marxian (as in Groucho, Harpo, and Chico) "The Trial Of The Chicago 7" has a bit of the prankster in it.
reviews.author: Michael Calleri

reviews.text: A powerful and relevant historic legal drama. Sorkin's script doesn't disappoint and his direction is better here. Plus, the cast is incredible. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fico Cangiano

reviews.text: The dialogue's crisp and cutting, the courtroom action is compelling, and the case for speaking truth to power and standing up for what's right springs to life in all its glory on the screen.
reviews.author: Rebecca Murray

reviews.text: One of the year's most watchable and well acted releases, tragically marred by Aaron Sorkin's failings as a director, not to mention his frustratingly middle of the road politics.
reviews.author: Dominic Griffin

reviews.text: Even if a couple of the characters get short shrift, the film's examination of the impact of protest is both fascinating and eerily timely.
reviews.author: Mike McGranaghan

reviews.text: The Trial of the Chicago 7 is timely, gripping, entertaining, moving, and a very important film to watch.
reviews.author: Marianna Neal

reviews.text: 'The Trial of the Chicago 7' argues that 1968 and 2020 aren't so different.
reviews.author: Jeff Mitchell

reviews.text: The verdict on "The Trial of the Chicago 7" is 'compelling,' beyond a reasonable doubt.'
reviews.author: Russ Simmons

reviews.text: Langella steals the show with an effective performance that will make you want to throw something at your TV. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ricardo Gallegos

reviews.text: It's really well done, it's really well-written, but it's limited by the fact that we know exactly what happened... It's as good as a movie like this can be, but it's not great.
reviews.author: Wade Major

reviews.text: It's classic Sorkin in that it illuminates and elucidates a [subject] matter that would have otherwise been opaque and confusing, but it's a little too Rashômon-like in that you never get the full master view of the riots... Good Sorkin, not great Sorkin.
reviews.author: Lael Loewenstein

reviews.text: It may be messy, but it's fleet-footed and it means well, and in the way of any good caper flick it extols the virtue of breaking the law for all the right reasons, come what may.
reviews.author: Melanie McFarland

reviews.text: With a wonderful cast and fairly solid writing and directing from Sorkin, there is a rousing call here that gives The Trial of the Chicago 7 power beyond being simply a good movie, and makes it one to look out for.
reviews.author: Kevin Lever

reviews.text: While The Trial of Chicago 7 got lucky with its release date, the film's relevance is owed to the endurance of the belief it's trying to tear down.
reviews.author: Jeva Lange

reviews.text: The most revelatory performance would be Sacha Baron Cohen's turn as Abbie Hoffman.
reviews.author: Randall King

reviews.text: The Trial of the Chicago 7 is a riveting movie...
reviews.author: Andrew R. Chow

reviews.text: This is a moving and powerful drama that rightly honors its titular subjects while opening audiences' eyes to the numerous parallels between the past and the present.
reviews.author: Grant Hermanns

reviews.text: The themes could not be more relevant to today...can justice prevail with a biased judge in charge?
reviews.author: Lisa Nesselson

reviews.text: Sorkin delivers his usual...but surprisingly gifted behind the camera as well...
reviews.author: Shawn Edwards

reviews.text: Yahya Abdul-Mateen II, Sacha Baron Cohen, Eddie Redmayne, Joseph Gordon-Levitt, Mark Rylance and Frank Langella deliver electrifying performances.
reviews.author: Saibal Chatterjee

reviews.text: We appreciate the stand that Cohen takes when he takes the stand. "Do you have contempt for your government?""I think the institutions of our democracy are wonderful things that are right now populated by some terrible people."
reviews.author: Jason Fraley

reviews.text: An utterly wonderful, vivid dramatization of the trial of Chicago's 1968 demonstrators, with bravura performances.
reviews.author: Tim Appelo

reviews.text: There's so much to revel in this film.
reviews.author: George M. Thomas

reviews.text: With his second directorial effort, Aaron Sorkin has produced a thoughtful meditation on a truly nightmarish event.
reviews.author: Zaki Hasan

reviews.text: Similar to [Sorkin's] approach to Molly's Game, dialogue supersedes other modes of conveying a story. This very intellectual reinterpretation is fact-filled to the point of being dense. Yet it is emotionally charged enough to be compelling.
reviews.author: Dwight Brown

reviews.text: Sorkin has offered up a ridiculously riveting, masterfully crafted, brilliantly acted, and astonishingly executed work. Most definitely the best film of 2020 to date...
reviews.author: Frank J. Avella

reviews.text: It represents the sanctification of a time and a people whose spirit Sorkin sees as our salvation.
reviews.author: Peter Rainer

reviews.text: All of Sorkin's dialogue leads to excellent performances from the entire ensemble. There isn't a weak link in the bunch and at the same time, there isn't a standout as so many of them get moments to shine.
reviews.author: Paul McGuire Grimes

reviews.text: This is the kind of film with all the semblance of a prestige blockbuster that could have arrived back in the 90s or 80s and been met with massive acclaim and box office.
reviews.author: Aaron Neuwirth

reviews.text: Like a good book, this is a real page turner. Aaron Sorkin is the master of fast-paced, cutting dialogue making it suit each character in this recreation of a turbulent time, not unlike the contentious climate we live in now.
reviews.author: Linda and Al Lerner

reviews.text: Many of the acclaimed scribe's usual flourishes and flashes of genius are present, of course, but there's a sense that this is a man pushing himself a little too far.
reviews.author: Tom Beasley

reviews.text: Aaron Sorkin revives the art of riveting courtroom drama with The Trial of the Chicago 7
reviews.author: Dustin Chase

reviews.text: The fall awards season roars in with this cinema powder keg. Expect Oscar to sprinkle gold dust on Aaron Sorkin and a gangbusters cast for making this recreation of a notorious 1969 trial burn with a timely relevance that singes the screen.
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: Aaron Sorkin and an incredible cast bring one of the most relevant movies of the year. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jesus Agudo

reviews.text: An engaging look at a tumultuous period in our history that proves we haven't evolved much if any since then. (Full Content Review for Parents - Violence, Profanity, etc. - also Available)
reviews.author: Jim Judy

reviews.text: The Trial of the Chicago 7﻿ makes for an entertaining and compelling courtroom drama, bolstered by Sorkin's script and strong performances.
reviews.author: Chris Agar

reviews.text: More than anything, Sorkin's film underscores the sacrifice these men made and applauds their willingness to stand up for what's right as the world crumbled around them.
reviews.author: Charles Koplinski

reviews.text: Sorkin's latest directorial offering is timely, engaging and undeniably thought-provoking. It is also spectacularly acted across the board.
reviews.author: Sara Michelle Fetters

reviews.text: Sorkin's film is sometimes eloquent, and sustained for the most part by his flair for hyperverbal entertainment. Yet it also diminishes its aura of authenticity with dubious inventions, and muddles its impact by taking on more history than it can handle.
reviews.author: Joe Morgenstern

reviews.text: The Trial of the Chicago 7 is one of the best films of the year and may be one of Sorkin's best of all time.
reviews.author: Pamela Powell

reviews.text: As it arrives on what Sorkin called "a collision course with history," it is both a cautionary tale and a guiding light out of the darkness.
reviews.author: Nell Minow

reviews.text: The Trial of the Chicago 7 is a master class in writing and acting. Writer/director Aaron Sorkin has crafted a compelling courtroom drama with a talented cast that could well be the best ensemble we will see in a film this year.
reviews.author: Micheal Compton

reviews.text: Classic Sorkin, down to the courtroom setting. It's a fairly traditional, all-star telling of a radical moment in history that aims to please and mostly does.
reviews.author: Abby Olcese

reviews.text: To paraphrase Bob Dylan, the times are indeed a-changin', but Sorkin's brand of sharp writing about politics, media, and culture hasn't gone out of style.
reviews.author: Brian Lowry

reviews.text: The Trial of the Chicago 7 is a cracking piece of entertainment, but it also serves as an easily accessible menu of ways to fight against oppression
reviews.author: Oscar Goff

reviews.text: Aaron Sorkin's artistic strengths are here slotted into the most basic form of Oscar bait.
reviews.author: Leigh Monson

reviews.text: All the usual suspects are here: snappy and acid-tongued dialogues as well as sardonic wits that Sorkin clearly has a field day making "The Trial of the Chicago 7" a courtroom circus both literally and figuratively.
reviews.author: Casey Chong

reviews.text: "The Trial of the Chicago 7" isn't good, but I'd recommend it anyway.
reviews.author: Chris Hewitt

reviews.text: Distortions notwithstanding, The Trial of the Chicago 7 is a rousing reminder of what was at stake in the late 1960s.
reviews.author: Alan Zilberman

reviews.text: A fire historical courtroom drama that's going to have so many people feeling all types of ways about the past and present in the fight for rights in the United States, from politics, police, race, etc. or, you know, just another Tuesday.
reviews.author: Julian Lytle

reviews.text: In his screenplay, Sorkin does a masterful job of picking through months of testimony to find significant exchanges that speak a universal language about the corruption of power and the desire to silence opposition voices.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: Sorkin, who's unmatched in his ability to write debates and speeches, manages to freshen up those old benches, robes and gavels.
reviews.author: Johnny Oleksinski

reviews.text: It has all the moral force of someone who spends their days writing sarcastic replies to Trump's tweets, all the while he tears down democracy piece by piece.
reviews.author: Clarisse Loughrey

reviews.text: The movie puts the past on the stand to inform the present - and also to galvanize it.
reviews.author: Peter Howell

reviews.text: A fine recreation of a certain moment in history that still feels relevant and timely ... even if it's heavy at times.
reviews.author: Edward Douglas

reviews.text: Showcases both Aaron Sorkin's great skill and his great shortcomings...telling the true story of a rambunctious American kangaroo court trial.
reviews.author: Matt Oakes

reviews.text: Now is not the time for nuance, it's the time for films such as The Trial of the Chicago 7 - films that wear their heart, and their humanism, on their sleeves.
reviews.author: Rohan Naahar

reviews.text: A compelling re-creation of a notorious trial that galvanized and even defined the 1960s.
reviews.author: Rafer Guzman

reviews.text: The trial moves along nicely and is so surprising that it is fun to watch. All the performances are good
reviews.author: Rachel Wagner

reviews.text: Sorkin has delivered a well-conceived, fast-paced account of one of the most heinous and controversial trials in American history.
reviews.author: Jeanne Kaplan

reviews.text: THE TRIAL OF THE CHICAGO 7 is truly an entertaining, spirited and relevant film that touches on a whole range of emotions.
reviews.author: David Kaplan

reviews.text: A smart, angry movie.
reviews.author: Randy Myers

reviews.text: I'm predicting right here and right now that Yahya Abdul Mateen is on his way to a second EMMY with his powerful role as Bobby Seale. Aaron Sorkin strikes on all cylinders with a timely, insightful film reminding us of WHY we protest in this country.
reviews.author: Carla Renata

reviews.text: The Trial of the Chicago 7 is right up there with the best, a film for the day, a film for the year, a film for the ages.
reviews.author: Lisa Johnson Mandell

reviews.text: Barn-burning speeches are a lot more rousing when the barn in question is rotted enough to require immediate burning to the ground.
reviews.author: Dana Stevens

reviews.text: Of course it's delightful to get to watch a snappy courtroom drama, offering some terrific actors, all getting a chance to shine, but, as he often does, Aaron Sorkin has a lot more on his mind.
reviews.author: Joanna Langfield

reviews.text: Perhaps more than any other film he's authored to date, Chicago 7 is a Sorkin experiment... and it might be his most interrogative screenplay of the ideals he so reveres.
reviews.author: David Crow

reviews.text: The Trial of the Chicago 7 mostly plays to Sorkin's strengths as writer, and sees him making great leaps forward as director.
reviews.author: Sean Mulvihill

reviews.text: An extremely powerful film that is, unfortunately, very relevant right now. There were moments that were almost too cringy to watch, but still important to see.
reviews.author: Tessa Smith

reviews.text: The Trial of Chicago 7 is less a chapter in history than a first draft still being written today, and Sorkin asks us all to take a stand for civil rights, even if it means taking THE stand.
reviews.author: Asher Luberto

reviews.text: For the most part, Sorkin's solid - if squarely made and visually uninteresting - film is a valuable contribution to the discourse of this election season.
reviews.author: Richard Lawson

reviews.text: Sorkin captures the period and issues well, while being alert to connections with our own fractious era, and the fantastic ensemble keeps you engaged when the writer's verbosity begins to become wearing.
reviews.author: Stephen Applebaum

reviews.text: It's a courtroom drama for sure, but what makes it special is that it's a courtroom drama from Aaron Sorkin.
reviews.author: Tom Santilli

reviews.text: Sorkin further proves his aplomb for courtroom dramas and snappy dialogue, and receives significant help from an astoundingly good ensemble.
reviews.author: Edwin Arnaudin

reviews.text: This movie should be seen by everyone before the election just to remind us of the dangers of an imperialistic president who thinks he's above the law.
reviews.author: Roger Friedman

reviews.text: "The Trial of the Chicago 7," the epitome of excellence, comes at just the right time: to show today's protestors some of the shoulders on which they stand.
reviews.author: Martha K. Baker

reviews.text: The Trial of the Chicago 7 is an ever-relevant and riveting tale of systemic corruption, buoyed by excellent performances and another fast-paced Aaron Sorkin script.
reviews.author: Lewis Knight

reviews.text: Sorkin's talent, distinct and unmistakable, drops a pearl into every exchange.
reviews.author: Mick LaSalle

reviews.text: Sorkin does a great job condensing a trial that lasted nearly five months and whose transcript totaled 22,000 pages into an engrossing two-hour movie.
reviews.author: Adrian Hennigan

reviews.text: It makes for an emotionally tough watch - though an exhilarating one too, given the torque of Sorkin's talk.
reviews.author: Jamie Graham

reviews.text: All in all, I plead guilty to enjoying this courtroom drama.
reviews.author: Dulcie Pearce

reviews.text: Much as Arthur Miller used the Salem witch trials of "The Crucible" to speak to the political witch trials of the McCarthy era, Sorkin ... methodically and passionately retells this 50-year-old trial to call attention to what's happening now.
reviews.author: Sean P. Means

reviews.text: The film looks to the role of protest and the government's reaction to it in a way that is enlightening as we face new protests now.
reviews.author: Beth Accomando

reviews.text: Sorkin can write, we all know this...there's an interesting drama in here, with a star-studded cast, but I'm not as knocked out as some people are. I enjoyed it, but it does have a pantomime quality to it, feeling fluffy...
reviews.author: Mark Kermode

reviews.text: When it clicks, it's gangbusters, with Sorkin's signature rat-a-tat dialogue bouncing between the actors like a pinball.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: It's a crackling production that captures an embarrassing moment in history.
reviews.author: Steven Prokopy

reviews.text: Sorkin has long demonstrated his ability to translate political theory into thrilling drama (just look at The West Wing), but here he elevates his game to new heights.
reviews.author: Joseph Walsh

reviews.text: Perfectly formed sentences fly like argument-seeking missiles, as characters stride purposefully towards the quickly retreating camera.
reviews.author: Brian Viner

reviews.text: Sorkin's drama, leavened by Abbie Hoffman's sitcom-style repartee and bloody vintage newsreel footage, can serve as a useful reminder that the more things change, the more they remain the same.
reviews.author: Kelly Vance

reviews.text: All arguing all the time, which plays to Sorkin's strengths as a writer, though his directorial chops are still undeveloped. And he doesn't have much of a point...but you can appreciate the work the actors do to make their characters more than types...
reviews.author: Norman Wilner

reviews.text: After a mediocre directorial debut, Aaron Sorkin has returned with a stellar historical film that doesn't overstate itself.
reviews.author: Stephen Silver

reviews.text: Leave it to Aaron Sorkin to take history, add a dozen "'West Wing' moments" and turn "The Trial of the Chicago 7" into a riveting dissertation on our nation's belly flop into the shallow end of fascism.
reviews.author: Al Alexander

reviews.text: ...the performances and byplay (a Sorkin specialty) give the movie plenty of burn.
reviews.author: Robert Denerstein

reviews.text: It's maybe a too little rosy, considering all that's going on, but The Trial of the Chicago 7 captures the messiness of this historical incident, all with that Sorkin panache.
reviews.author: Esther Zuckerman

reviews.text: The Trial of the Chicago 7 sees a mature Sorkin back on form with all the punch and momentum of his better work, while maintaining a welcome degree of control over his most idiosyncratic tics.
reviews.author: Christopher Machell

reviews.text: "Chicago 7" may be a bit too familiar and user friendly at times, but if there was ever a moment to take it all in again, it would be now.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: The truth of this sad episode in American history is a tad too strange and bloated to lend itself to a compelling theatrical adaptation, but Sorkin and his talented stars do the best they can with the material
reviews.author: J. Don Birnam

reviews.text: Necessary right now, to remind us that if we have a constitution, it should apply to ALL AMERICANS. The genius is the expression of what this trial meant ... and means today!
reviews.author: Patrick McDonald

reviews.text: A real life drama that would have benefited with more realism. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jorge Iván Morales

reviews.text: Sacha Baron Cohen steals the show in Aaron Sorkin's mostly entertaining, occasionally cheesy, totally timely take on a notorious US trial.
reviews.author: Charlotte O'Sullivan

reviews.text: Writer-director Aaron Sorkin assembles an A-list cast to chronicle the powerful story which parallels the current climate as political unrest once again sweeps across the nation.
reviews.author: Joe Friar

reviews.text: Aaron Sorkin's timely screenplay strikingly points out the parallel of then and now.
reviews.author: Robin Clifford

reviews.text: This is a film that examines both the past and the present day; that plots a path on the common ground between them.
reviews.author: Wendy Ide

reviews.text: [T]he compassionate, optimistic and indeed counterintuitive ending feels like the aspirational balm that we need right now.
reviews.author: Kevin Maher

reviews.text: It's a project tailor-made for Aaron Sorkin [that] was surely catnip to write. No wonder its 129-minute runtime flies by like nothing.
reviews.author: Jared Mobarak

reviews.text: Sorkin's winks are so shameless that you can hear them flutter across your own living room, but that doesn't make them unenjoyable, either.
reviews.author: Barry Hertz

reviews.text: Sorkin avoids his usual verbal density for an elegant, persuasive and mature film that hits all the right notes.
reviews.author: Anne Brodie

reviews.text: Sorkin does a commendable job of getting the dramatic feel mostly right - including the demented rage of the notorious Judge Hoffman (wonderfully played by Frank Langella) and the dislike between Hayden and Hoffman.
reviews.author: Jim Slotek

reviews.text: Few celebrations of a radical impulse have been so conciliatory to bourgeois convention.
reviews.author: Donald Clarke

reviews.text: When it all clicks, its terrific cast in full flow in the packed courtroom, it's truly stirring stuff.
reviews.author: Philip De Semlyen

reviews.text: It's...competently directed and buoyed by a handful of powerhouse performances, occasionally zippy dialogue, and some excellent wigs.
reviews.author: Gena Radcliffe

reviews.text: It's Oscars-bait galore in this star-studded courtroom drama from Aaron Sorkin.
reviews.author: Larushka Ivan-Zadeh

reviews.text: The film, with most of the drama unfolding in court (the riots is in flashbacks), is a lean, mean sizzler, taut at every turn.
reviews.author: Tom Meek

reviews.text: Flashbacks are used judiciously and events build and turn nicely towards a real cliffhanger, one that will put you on the edge of your seat and hanging off every word.
reviews.author: James Croot

reviews.text: [T]he film (which actually started life as a vehicle for Spielberg) reveals itself to be sloppy, sanctimonious and worse, meaningless.
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: When you have Aaron Sorkin writing and directing you can't go wrong.
reviews.author: Jackie K. Cooper

reviews.text: Somehow, the gross miscarriage of justice against innocent men has been made into a cracking good time.
reviews.author: Charles Bramesco

reviews.text: A terrifying film at its core thanks to its display of despicable politics within the law system, The Trial of the Chicago 7 is another 2020 necessity.
reviews.author: Peter Gray

reviews.text: A compelling courtroom drama brought to life by a masterful ensemble cast and Sorkin's penchant for firecracker dialogue, 'The Trial of the Chicago 7' is a period melodrama dripping in modern pertinency.
reviews.author: Doug Jamieson

reviews.text: It bridges the past to the present without being too obvious or coy about its goals, and that might be Sorkin's greatest achievement with his latest.
reviews.author: Andrew Parker

reviews.text: Aaron Sorkin's The Trial of the Chicago 7 may not be the squarest film ever made about 1960s radicalism... Still, this loose "true story" is exactly what you would expect from Sorkin.
reviews.author: Jake Wilson

reviews.text: Sorkin has no plan for the camera beyond pointing it at his stars, but he lets their performances grow large and moreish.
reviews.author: Danny Leigh

reviews.text: Much of the film's appeal lies in its brilliantly snappy dialogue. Having said that, those who remain unconvinced by Sorkin's particular brand of witty repartee won't find anything here that's likely to change their minds.
reviews.author: Linda Marric

reviews.text: "The Trial of the Chicago 7" moves with an electric purpose, and it will be hard to escape the parallels the project has to offer to today's culture.
reviews.author: Matthew Passantino

reviews.text: The direction in 'Trial' is efficient but glossy. The writing is precise, but maybe a little too precise.
reviews.author: Jordan Ruimy

reviews.text: "If you want to listen to the creator of The West Wing mansplain the 1960s to you, then The Trial of The Chicago 7 is your dream project."
reviews.author: Neal Pollack

reviews.text: Although not all the notes are sterling and it's surprisingly not as dark as it could be, it's another necessary and well-crafted reminder of the grueling struggle to protect freedoms by speaking truth to power, even though it often falls on deaf ears.
reviews.author: Nicholas Bell

reviews.text: This momentous cultural event from the end of the turbulent 60's is apt to floor those unfamiliar with the case given the uncanny similarities with events today... The film features a dynamic, sprawling ensemble, one of the best of the year.
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: The Trial of the Chicago 7 may be more interesting than much of the other films about this period, but it also only feels like the tip of the iceberg...
reviews.author: Ryan Silberstein

reviews.text: Above all, the film shines in... the tension between Hoffman and Hayden. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Andrea G. Bermejo

reviews.text: Putting you through the wringer with every twist and turn, it's a powerful, enraging and pertinent evocation of what you're up against when the establishment is the enemy.
reviews.author: Emma Simmonds

reviews.text: It plays to Sorkin's strengths and those of his ensemble, while delivering the spirited call-to-arms that will reverberate louder right now than in any other moment in time.
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: A witty, charming, crowd-pleasing courtroom drama that's passionately performed by a terrific ensemble and expertly edited for maximum impact.
reviews.author: Shaun Munro

reviews.text: "The Trial of the Chicago 7" offers an absorbing primer in a chapter of American history that was both bizarre and ruefully meaningful.
reviews.author: Ann Hornaday

reviews.text: Well told by Sorkin, and acted fantastically across the board. And what it has to say about justice, the fragility of our democracy, and the abuses by those running this nation couldn't be timelier.
reviews.author: Jeff York

reviews.text: As a director, Sorkin proves to be more effective in his work with the actors and he does a very good job of juggling his enormous cast of characters.
reviews.author: Peter Sobczynski

reviews.text: 28 years after Sorkin wrote A Few Good Men, he returns with yet another blistering courtroom drama.
reviews.author: Mike Ryan

reviews.text: Netflix has another hot awards contender! Sorkin delivers another searing script, and as a director gets top notch performances from his cast across the board. Very timely!
reviews.author: Grace Randolph

reviews.text: "The Trial of the Chicago 7" is one of the most entertaining courtroom dramas in years.
reviews.author: Jonathan W. Hickman

reviews.text: This film is one of those exhilarating instances when Sorkin finds a context in which all of his well-established impulses that can be so annoying elsewhere...
reviews.author: Alison Willmore

reviews.text: The Trial of the Chicago 7 is Sorkin's second time working behind the camera, and his direction feels remarkably more assured than his debut effort, but where the film truly shines are in its superb ensemble cast, and its dialogue.
reviews.author: Brent Hankins

reviews.text: My only objection is that it almost looks like men were mainly the ones fighting for civil rights in the '60s. I'm sure Sorkin could have found a good C.J. Cregg -- The West Wing's talented press secretary -- for this story. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Patricia Puentes

reviews.text: Aaron Sorkin is back on his game in superbly cast "The Trial of the Chicago 7."
reviews.author: James Verniere

reviews.text: Sorkin is as unsubtle as ever, but the high dramatics and contemporaneous relevance of The Trial of the Chicago 7 make for a nice fit with the writer-director's showman instincts.
reviews.author: Mattie Lucas

reviews.text: There are such wonderful individual moments and beats in  that just watching it as an acting exercise makes it worthwhile.
reviews.author: Brian Tallerico

reviews.text: [T]his specific story and its implications deserve a radical approach, and Sorkin's is as centrist and lacking in self-awareness as it is full of hot air.
reviews.author: Matt Cipolla

reviews.text: Powerhouse acting and Sorkin's usual crackling dialogue make this a must-see.
reviews.author: Chris Bumbray

reviews.text: A stellar cast leads The Trial of the Chicago 7 into special territory. Sorkin knows how to pitch the dialogue, and his performers willing step into the actor's showcase.
reviews.author: Alan French

reviews.text: The Trial of the Chicago 7' is an exhilarating piece of courtroom drama, and the starry cast makes the weighty script fly off the screen.
reviews.author: Brian Lloyd

reviews.text: A fiery condemnation of the police state and government overreach, this is both timely and timeless. Sorkin and a superb cast make legal proceedings compelling, and then show that the law is an ass.
reviews.author: Helen O'Hara

reviews.text: The Trial of the Chicago 7 is a supremely impactful film. It finds a pitch-perfect balance between levity, humor, and bluntness.
reviews.author: Ben Rolph

reviews.text: A good legal drama with comedic touches that could -and should- have been great. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Nestor Bentancor

reviews.text: Despite Sorkin's significant shortcomings as a director, The Trial of the Chicago 7 hums along mightily on the strength of its god-tier ensemble and whip-smart script. There's hardly a false note in the cast.
reviews.author: Clint Worthington

reviews.text: The film is exactly what it needs to be -- an assertive and impassioned piece of political theater.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: This is a powerful broadside from one of Hollywood's most talented writers that you won't want to miss.
reviews.author: James Mottram

reviews.text: Timely and sharp, 'The Trial of the Chicago 7' unravels a gripping courtroom yarn.
reviews.author: Preston Barta

reviews.text: The Trial of the Chicago 7 represents a brilliant example of what cinema can do. A period piece that's just as vital today.
reviews.author: Joey Magidson

reviews.text: The Trial of the Chicago 7 details events that happened more than 50 years ago. The time to look away is never.
reviews.author: Stephanie Zacharek

reviews.text: The Trial of the Chicago 7 is a new masterpiece from Aaron Sorkin.
reviews.author: Danielle Solzman

reviews.text: The Trial Of The Chicago 7 wants to bottle the revolutionary spirit of its setting-the take-to-the-streets idealism of the '60s-but its snappy montage-glimpses of demonstrations verge on costume-party kitsch.
reviews.author: A.A. Dowd

reviews.text: It's talky and clumsy, alternating between self-importance and clowning. But it's also not a movie that can be easily shaken off. Partly this is an accident of timing.
reviews.author: A.O. Scott

reviews.text: [A]gain and again, scenes and lines land with a solemn clunk.
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

reviews.text: Aaron Sorkin and a superb cast deliver a warning shot from the past with extreme importance resonance for Trump's America in which we are living now.
reviews.author: Pete Hammond

reviews.text: "Trial" is so inherently compelling - and so directly germane to an America where the government labels cities "anarchist jurisdictions" and states are drawing up laws against free assembly - that it doesn't need the frills.
reviews.author: Ty Burr

reviews.text: As the didactic prankster [Abbie Hoffman], Sacha Baron Cohen is a revelation.
reviews.author: Rubin Safaya

reviews.text: Breezy for a serious topic, "The Trial of the Chicago 7" is something unexpected, fun.
reviews.author: Bill Goodykoontz

reviews.text: [A] remarkably relevant story, smartly told, but with certain blind spots and pitfalls: broad strokes, rhetorical grandstanding, the tendency to overstuff an already load-bearing tale.
reviews.author: Leah Greenblatt

reviews.text: "The Trial of the Chicago 7," smoothly entertaining as it is, may also elude clear consensus.
reviews.author: Justin Chang

reviews.text: Crackling dialogue and excellent performances make for a captivating exploration of a complicated subject, but the film never totally coheres.
reviews.author: Matt Goldberg

reviews.text: Sorkin's writing may be better served by a director who can bring a new set of perspectives and dynamics to the work, rather than simply presenting them head-on. Yet it works anyway.
reviews.author: Michael Phillips

reviews.text: Aaron Sorkin makes a triumphant return to the courtroom with a terrific ensemble in "The Trial of the Chicago 7," which packs a timely, relevant punch, showcasing both the mood of our country and the power of protest.
reviews.author: Nate Adams

reviews.text: The Trial of the Chicago 7 is nothing if not a showcase for great performances.
reviews.author: Chris Evangelista

reviews.text: The best film that the barren 2020 cinematic landscape has given way to, and certainly the best original feature in Netflix's continually strengthening lineup.
reviews.author: Kyle Pinion

reviews.text: It's slick, well-assembled Hollywood entertainment that should entertain as it educates, and hopefully infuriates, its audiences.
reviews.author: Sean O'Connell

reviews.text: The filmmaker crafts an entertaining, immersive and ultimately optimistic spectacle that never forgets, especially at its ending, that humanity should always trump the system.
reviews.author: Brian Truitt

reviews.text: A look back at rabble-rousers from another era won't change the world, but "Chicago 7" is a solid tribute to a few men who realized they could, even when the system they fought for came up short.
reviews.author: Eric Kohn

reviews.text: [I]t's a thoroughly satisfying drama whose emotional climax hinges on an implied possessive pronoun, of all things.
reviews.author: Steve Pond

reviews.text: Make no mistake, just because it is heightened for dramatic effect, it is no less evocative as the manipulation of our justice system to favor those who wield and wish to maintain that power continues to this day.
reviews.author: Douglas Davidson

reviews.text: Aaron Sorkin's "The Trial of the Chicago 7" is the rare drama about the 1960s that's powerful and authentic and moving enough to feel as if it were taking place today.
reviews.author: Owen Gleiberman

reviews.text: While the film ends on something of a movie-of-the-week note, given the timing of its release as a current Department of Justice gins up spurious charges against political enemies, it nevertheless carries a certain past-is-prologue immediacy.
reviews.author: Chris Barsanti

reviews.text: Every clash of differences only tightens the cohesions of their unified cause and thickens the performances and, for a Sorkin film, you can bet every syllable is measured to millisecond for maximum effect.
reviews.author: Don Shanahan

reviews.text: Aaron Sorkin is absolutely on fire here, revisiting his courtroom drama A Few Good Men roots and crafting a Molotov cocktail for the moment in cinematic form
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: This is not a documentary; it's a dramatization of events that resonates with great power while containing essential truths, and it's one of the best movies of the year.
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: Through a punch-the-air final act, Aaron Sorkin's melodrama reassures us of the power of sticking to one's beliefs
reviews.author: Robert Daniels

reviews.text: Sorkin has made a movie that's gripping, illuminating and trenchant, as erudite as his best work and always grounded first and foremost in story and character.
reviews.author: David Rooney

synopsis: In 1969, seven people were charged by the federal government with conspiracy and more, arising from the protests at the 1968 Democratic National Convention in Chicago.
